title: Epistemology Lens Switch
summary: One fictional school reports a rise in low-level classroom disruption, and the same evidence is given to three research teams with different assumptions about what the social world is. Learners declare a realist/positivist, critical realist or social constructionist starting point and then make five decisions - research object, legitimate question, admissible evidence, method, defensible claim - watching the specification and its coherence change as they go. Running a second lens on the same case produces a side-by-side comparison of what each design makes visible, what it hides and what action it points to.
learningObjectives: State what a realist/positivist, a critical realist and a social constructionist study each take the research object to be.
Explain why the method follows from assumptions about the object rather than the other way round.
Identify the precise claim a given design could support about the same case, and the claim it could not.
Distinguish social construction from fabrication, and coherence from truth.
Recognise when an explanation has been relocated into individuals before any data were collected.
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; every judgement is evaluated in the browser tab, and the tool asks nothing about the person using it.
accessibilityNotes: Native radios, buttons and fieldsets throughout; no dragging and no timing. Only one decision is expanded at a time and collapsing is done by toggling the hidden attribute rather than rebuilding, so keyboard focus survives; focus moves deliberately to the first option of a decision only when a navigation button is pressed. Coherence is always written out in words ('follows from your position', 'in tension') as well as tinted, so no state depends on colour. The study specification is a table, not a diagram, so it needs no chart alternative. Changes are announced through the shell's polite live region; reduced motion is honoured; forced-colours rules are provided; the layout is usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths.
readmeTopic: Same school, same evidence, three epistemologies: how the research object decides the method and the defensible claim
simulationNotes: Meadowbank Academy, its incident counts, staff survey, behaviour policy revision, room moves and focus-group quotations are invented for teaching and estimate nothing. There is no random generation and no seed: the tool is deterministic. Coherence is scored simply as the number of the five decisions whose home position matches the declared position, and the tool states in the interface that this is a minimum standard rather than a measure of quality. Each decision offers a fourth option belonging to a person-centred realism that is not one of the three declared positions; it is included because it is the design a school is most likely to fund, and it is named rather than merely penalised. Three positions is a deliberate simplification of a contested landscape and the tool does not rank them: each lens profile carries what it makes visible and what it costs.
